items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: my wife drove Frank Sinatra’s car, because Nancy couldn’t drive.

ctx.x: It’s too bad that those things disappeared because I guess the dancing was so connected to the music.

Well the dancing was connected to ballrooms also, see? So that’s what made bands play the ballrooms, because dancing was there rather than, in some hotels, yes, big hotels would have a band like we played the Hotel Sherman — I can’t think of the name of the room. Anyway, what’d I say, the Hotel Sherman? In Chicago. And the Oriental Theatre there, Chicago Theatre there. And that was our stop in Chicago, and then from there we went to California. So we did a series of one-nighters. Now my wife drove Frank Sinatra’s…
